phase3_findings.description: scripts/review-context-eval.py:153 _usage_field: a transcript record carrying a non-finite token value (json.loads accepts bare Infinity/-Infinity by default) reaches int(float('inf')) and raises OverflowError, which subclasses ArithmeticError and is NOT in the per-record backstop's caught tuple (AttributeError, TypeError, ValueError, KeyError) at line 376 — detonating the whole corpus walk. Confirmed by reproduction. Violates the module's own 'degrades per malformed record without detonating' contract and the spirit of AC5. Asymmetric with NaN, which raises ValueError and IS caught. Real defect; not merge-blocking (maintainer-only instrument, requires adversarial/corrupt transcript never emitted by the real harness; identical pattern exists in the already-merged implement sibling). Fix: reject non-finite floats in _usage_field or add ArithmeticError to the caught tuple.

docs/internal/review-context.md:13-14 states the page 'is not paraphrased in DEVFLOW_SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md, which only points here' — but DEVFLOW_SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md contains no reference to review-context.md, review-context-eval, or #1852 (both sibling instruments ARE referenced there). The 'which only points here' clause is a false factual claim against HEAD, and the new page also breaks the repo's single-source-with-pointers convention. Real doc defect; not merge-blocking. Fix by adding the pointer to the overview in the same change, or rewording to 'and is not referenced from DEVFLOW_SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md'.

render_text's skip section (## Skipped records and files headline, per-reason lines, and the separate ## Dropped from an axis heading for unresolvable_read_path) is never exercised with a non-zero skip population, so the reader-facing surface AC5 requires is untested. Also untested: walk_error branch, _usage_field bool-rejection guard, aggregate total_usage_missing_turns field, and directory-symlink escape (safe only via os.walk followlinks=False default, which no test pins). Non-blocking coverage gaps.

scripts/review-context-eval.py:145-163 _usage_field accepts negative token counts, so a hostile negative input_tokens is summed into peak and reported as an established real (but wrong) number; and an empty-string file_path (a str) is silently treated as a non-engine non-count rather than tallied under unresolvable_read_path. Minor robustness gaps on a maintainer instrument.

The int|str UNESTABLISHED sentinel union is soundly handled by every consumer (aggregate filters it before arithmetic; render_text and json.dumps treat it opaquely). Sentinel is a bare string sharing type-space with data fields, and _median can widen the union to int|float|str; both are defensible pragmatic choices, not defects. No merge-blocking type-design issues.
